task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage with at least one organizer, shaper, terminal role
methodological_questions: How to define organizer, shaper, terminal roles from play-by-play data
How to measure lineup coverage across possession-level data
How to separate the effect of role coverage from overall player talent
How to implement within-team talent controls without lookahead

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality (pct_ran_BEST - pct_ran_AVOID) did not predict series wins after controlling for RS net-rating talent; corr(talent,adapt)=+0.124; talent predictor significant, adapt not; n~55 series; untestable due to confounding and small sample.

Named star initiators have identifiable lineup and forced-play-type suppressors in the possession graph; e.g. Jokic vs MIN PPP 0.814; no placebo or matching; later work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
Higher AVOID share was weakly associated with losing at series level (rho=-0.26 p=0.07, n=50) but still confounded by team quality; ~80 series needed for p<0.05; untestable with these data.
Execution conformance scoring for ORL vs DET in one game; descriptive only, no hypothesis test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Separating a coaching/strategic metric (adaptation quality) from talent in series-level prediction
failed_approaches.why: Confounding between adaptation and talent (corr=+0.124) and small sample (55 series) left adaptation non-significant after talent control

failed_approaches.what_failed: Isolating the effect of AVOID share on winning from team quality
failed_approaches.why: Team-quality confound persisted; series-level n=50 underpowered (needed ~80)

failed_approaches.what_failed: Superstar suppression by lineup without placebo validation
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts

evidence_establishes: No prior study directly tested lineup coverage with organizer[path] roles

Prior attempts to separate structural concepts (adaptation quality, AVOID share) from talent at the series level were confounded and underpowered, implying that talent control requires large within-unit samples and careful identification
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup coverage varies within teams
Whether coverage effects are separable from talent counts
Whether talent control 'behaves' in the presence of coverage metrics
own_inferences: The 420,993 possession-level observations across 90 team-seasons permit within-team (fixed-effect) models that can absorb overall team talent, addressing the confounding seen in earlier series-level studies
Roles (organizer, shaper, terminal) can be defined from a prior window (e.g., previous season or first half of season) to avoid lookahead leakage
The main remaining threats are measurement reliability of structural roles, possible base-rate ceilings if coverage prevalence is too high, and unobserved player-quality confounds at the lineup level
uncertainties: Reliability of role classifications derived from a single season's play-by-play when applied to that same season
Whether coach substitution patterns generate enough within-team variation in coverage to power the test
Stability of role classifications across game states (blowouts, clutch) and opponent quality

historical_effect.explanation: No directly relevant earlier study existed; the retrieved failures in separating structural metrics from talent at the series level highlight risks but do not change the decision, because the current question uses large-sample within-team variation that was not available in those series-level studies.

blocking_constraints.text: Talent confound may not be fully removed by within-team fixed effects if unobserved player skill interacts with role classification.
Structural role definitions for organizer[path] rely on noisy influence estimates; measurement error could bias coefficients.

prior_work.summary: No earlier study in the retrieved families addresses lineup coverage or the effect of having at least one organizer, shaper, and terminal player on offensive performance.

risks.text: Even with team fixed effects, within-team lineup performance may be confounded by the specific skills of the players who enable coverage.
Role labels derived from a single season's play-type initiations may misclassify borderline players, attenuating estimated effects.
If roles are computed using the same games as the performance outcome, future information leaks into the coverage indicator; must use a temporal split.
If coverage is very common (e.g., >80% of possessions), variation may be insufficient to precisely estimate effects.
Many possible role definitions and analysis windows increase risk of false positives unless a single pre-registered specification is used.

design.estimand: Effect of lineup coverage (binary: presence of ≥1 organizer, ≥1 shaper, ≥1 terminal scorer on the floor simultaneously) on offensive points per possession, controlling for team fixed effects and a composite talent measure of the five players.
design.unit: Posession or stint-level observation, excluding garbage time.
design.sample: NBA 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons (primary); 2025-26 as holdout for validation. Use all possessions where roles are defined from prior-season data (or first-half-of-season data in a robustness check).
design.power: >400,000 possessions; plausible effect size 0.015 PPP detectable with >0.80 power after within-team clustering, assuming a moderate intra-team correlation.
design.controls: Team fixed effects; sum of five offensive RAPM / EPM as talent proxy; game state (score margin, period); opponent defensive rating or fixed effects; home/away indicator.
design.falsification: 1. Role shuffle: randomly permute role labels within team across players; coverage effect should disappear. 2. Same-season leakage test: define roles from the same season as the outcome and compare coefficient to the out-of-sample definition. 3. Temporal split: define roles from first 41 games and test on second 41; reverse and compare.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary specification with role definition from previous season and within-team FE; report all other sensitivity checks as exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Primary test: one-sided p < 0.01 for coverage coefficient >0, using cluster-robust standard errors by lineup and team-season; also compute Bayesian posterior probability that coverage effect > 0.5 anticipated effect size.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play and derived possessions as of 2026-07-13; role definitions from Structural Influence pipeline v2 (usage median split + residual influence, using previous season data).
